_comment: Training presets, sized against measured throughput on the RTX 3060 in this
machine. `config` is a TrainConfig body: POST it to the engine's /train, or
save it through the backend's /training/presets to get it into the UI.
Sizing rule: Chinchilla puts the compute-optimal point at ~20 training tokens
per parameter. Parameters here means non-embedding — with a tied 8k-vocab
table the embedding is a lookup, not compute, and counting it would size the
corpus for arithmetic that never happens. `tokens` below is 20x non-embedding
and is trained for exactly one epoch, so the model never sees a token twice.
Every hours figure is the marginal step rate from a real loop.run over the
packed corpus, taken between report frames so compilation is excluded.
Repeat measurements on this card spread about 4%, so treat them as +/- 5%.
See README, 'Sizing a run', for how to derive another one.

presets.name: Chinchilla 1
presets.notes: The compute-optimal run that fits in an hour. 18.15M params, 14.48M non-embedding; 290M tokens at 20.0 per non-embedding parameter, one epoch, 35.4k steps, ~1.03h, 1.4 GiB VRAM. Needs a repack: the packed corpus is 391M tokens and this wants 290M, so rebuild_dataset is on and the FineWeb cap of 4070 files trims it. Budget 10-20 min for the tokenizer and pack before the first step.

presets.name: Chinchilla 1 (whole corpus)
presets.notes: The same rule applied to the corpus already on disk, so nothing is repacked. 23.10M params, 18.90M non-embedding; all 391M tokens at 20.7 per non-embedding parameter, one epoch, 47.7k steps, ~1.66h, 1.6 GiB VRAM. Two thirds of an hour over target buys 27% more model and skips the repack — the better first run unless the corpus is being changed anyway.

presets.name: Smoke
presets.notes: Deliberately not compute-optimal: 38M tokens against a 7.39M-parameter trunk is 5.2 per parameter, a quarter of Chinchilla. It exists to prove the pipeline end to end in ~5 minutes of training (4.7k steps at 320d/4h/6L), not to produce a model worth keeping. Repacks first, but only 500 FineWeb files, so the pack is quick too.
